correctness.rationale: The ordered intervals telescope to a normalized law, and every nontrivial upper tail at cumulative mass s is m(S−s)/(S(m+s)), with strictly positive derivative for 0<s<S. Independently calculated the variance using the pairwise identity sum_{i<j} p_i p_j (d_i−d_j)^2 and obtained both rational expressions in RESULT.md. The first derivative factor is monic with roots in (1,2) and (20,3858); the other has opposite-sign roots and its positive root lies in (2,20). All are simple and give +,−,+,− derivative signs, with positive roots 1.0736528591140186, 15.376434751062521, 3856.926347140886. For two distances the far probability increases strictly, so the derivative of its Bernoulli variance can vanish only when that probability reaches 1/2; a one-destination variance is constant and has no strict extrema. The theorem concerns real positive origin mass and conditional distance variance, not integer-sampled local extrema or trip counts. Read the supplied check.py and requirements.txt without executing them. Replay the independent algebra and numerical root check with `python3 /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py` (SymPy and mpmath; section 5 of stdout). Root isolation and the two-destination obstruction are analytic, not numerical extrapolations.

value.rationale: A mean-distance shift and a change in dispersion are different mobility-model diagnostics. A three-bin, exact maximum–minimum–maximum example despite strict outward stochastic order shows that even a repeated reversal is possible in the actual radiation family; the Bernoulli obstruction makes the support-size threshold interpretable and sharp. The result is an analytical model constraint, not empirical evidence or a classification of all triples.
